clue.text: Heroine, desolate, having difficulty on Exmoor at first

parts.note: lorn is an old word for forlorn or desolate
ado is fuss or trouble, a difficulty

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word Exmoor

explanation.surface: A heroine wanders, forlorn and in trouble, across the moors of the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel is set on Exmoor, a moor in south-west England, so the surface paints her own story.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Blackmore's romance is its central female figure.

clue.text: Fair goal

definitions.meaning: fair in the sense of impartial, unbiased
a goal is an aim or target

explanation.definitionFit: An impartial judgement is unbiased, and a target to aim for is also a noun of the same spelling.

clue.text: Picnic here, grabbing such a comfortable place

indicators.note: the phrase Picnic here grabbing a run of letters means they sit inside those words

explanation.surface: A picnicker settles on a cosy, sheltered spot for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug nook or recess where someone fits well is a comfortable spot.

clue.text: Return to base by car and push right in

definitions.meaning: to hammer a nail fully in, or press a point home

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to motor back to your house and to force something, such as a nail or argument, fully in.

clue.text: Collected works vehicle

definitions.meaning: a volume gathering several works together
an old word for a bus

explanation.definitionFit: A single volume of several books, and the older full name of a bus.

clue.text: Watching hunting without initial publicity

indicators.note: without tells us to take some letters away from the hunting word

parts.note: preying is hunting for food
PR, public relations, is publicity reduced to its initials

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a quiet hunt that has been kept out of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes PR (public relations, given as initials) from PREYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at something closely is observing it, a present participle like the clue word.

clue.text: Egyptian in need of firm physical exercise

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A man from Egypt needs a company gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the native Christian church of Egypt.

clue.text: Skipper with large vessel that's outside entrance

parts.note: Capt. abbreviates captain, the skipper

indicators.note: outside puts the letters for the phrase that's around the vessel

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
a vat is a large tub

explanation.surface: A ship's captain with a big boat moored by a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not a doorway; IE (that is) goes 'outside' VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to hold them spellbound.

clue.text: Indian detailed to analyse sentences

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its last letter cut off

parts.note: a Parsee is a Zoroastrian of Indian descent

explanation.surface: An Indian student is set a grammar exercise in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as de-tailed: lose the tail of PARSEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a sentence into its grammatical parts is a grammarian's task.

clue.text: Discharge dunderhead from the Blues

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so letters leave the gloom word

parts.note: the blues is low spirits, dejection
the head of the word dunder is its first letter D

explanation.surface: An idiot is thrown out of the Blues, a football or regimental side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool but is the head of dunder; 'the Blues' looks like a team but means low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing out or expelling is a discharge.

clue.text: Drift one mile to harbour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A boat drifts one mile toward the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drift' means the gist or meaning of something, not floating.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of a remark is its meaning or significance.

clue.text: Contrive to edge into church after start of service

indicators.note: after places the church part behind the service letter
start of picks out only the opening letter of service
into puts the edge word inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is an edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sidle into church once the service has begun.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot or devise a plan is to contrive one.

clue.text: Playing member of The Drones' club?

definitions.text: Playing member of The Drones' club?

parts.words: Playing member of The Drones' club?
parts.note: reads like a member of Wodehouse's idle gentlemen's club; really a musician whose instrument has drones

explanation.surface: A sporting member of a famous fictional London club for idle young men.
explanation.walkthrough: The Drones Club is Bertie Wooster's club in P. G. Wodehouse; drones are also the bass pipes of a Scottish instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on a Highland instrument plays one with drones.

clue.text: Quote a lot verbally

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: a sight, as in a sight better, means a lot

explanation.surface: A speaker quotes heavily from a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a source as evidence is to quote it.

clue.text: Extension for drawers

parts.note: reads like extra room for a chest of drawers; really added play for teams that have drawn

explanation.surface: A carpenter adds a bit more space to a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional minutes are played when a knockout match is level, extending it for the two drawing sides.

clue.text: Ritual braves once organised

indicators.note: organised means the letters of braves once are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Warriors once held an organised ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite or ceremonial custom is a ritual.

clue.text: It is hardly brilliant to cheat over crossword answer

indicators.note: over in a down clue sets the cheat word above the next part

parts.note: rush is old slang for cheating someone by overcharging
a light is a crossword solver's name for an answer in the grid

explanation.surface: Cheating on a crossword answer is hardly a brilliant move.
explanation.walkthrough: A rushlight was a cheap candle of a rush dipped in fat, giving a dim light.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush dipped in tallow gave only a feeble glimmer, far from bright.

clue.text: Urbane tip to get money annually for royalties

parts.note: civil means polite, urbane
to list is to lean or tip, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A polite hint about getting a yearly stipend for royal authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royalties' looks like authors' fees but means members of the royal family; the Civil List was Parliament's yearly grant to the British royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: The yearly sum Parliament voted for the monarch's household.

clue.text: Numbers lacking an initiation in the principles of art

indicators.note: lacking means the following letters are dropped from the numbing word

parts.note: anaesthetics are things that numb, numbers
the word an as the initial part of the word

explanation.surface: Counting skills are lacking in an art initiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' reads as figures but is things that numb.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophy of beauty and taste is the theory behind art.

clue.text: Fashionable drink, it's said, for one in the know

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: it's said marks that the drink word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Someone in the know orders a fashionable drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an inner circle has privileged knowledge.

clue.text: Messenger dropping off nothing — it's a sin

indicators.note: dropping off means letting a piece fall away from the messenger word

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A messenger falls asleep on duty, which is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' looks like nodding off but means losing the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy of another's fortune is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Doctor put girls on dark treacle

indicators.note: on sets the girls after the doctor in an across answer

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes dark treacle for some girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick dark syrup from sugar refining is a kind of treacle.

clue.text: University at one time without a lightweight

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the old-time word wraps the university letter

parts.note: once means at one time
U is university

explanation.surface: A university once had no lightweight boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Scorn food

definitions.meaning: slang for grub, something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to jeer, and the same spelling is slang for grub.

clue.text: Identifies sources of records

explanation.definitionFit: Tags name things, and record companies issue discs under such names.

clue.text: Villain's excellent!

definitions.meaning: an old word for a hired ruffian or desperado
a cry of approval, well done

explanation.definitionFit: A hired desperado in older usage, and a cheer of approval.

clue.text: One doing badly as a blue

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: badly means the letters of doing are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone doing poorly feels blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blue' looks like a mood but is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep violet-blue is one colour of the rainbow.

clue.text: Arrogant cur I caught pinching rug

parts.note: a cur is a dog
a mat is a small rug
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An arrogant mongrel and I were caught stealing a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserting opinions as certain truth is overbearing and arrogant.

clue.text: Announced top dog

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: The top dog at a show is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' reads as one phrase, but 'top' is the homophone piece and 'dog' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small toy breed of dog.

clue.text: Arrives before anyone else For Scottish celebration

definitions.text: Arrives before anyone else For Scottish celebration

parts.words: Arrives before anyone else For Scottish celebration
parts.note: describes being the earliest guest across the threshold at a Hogmanay New Year party

explanation.surface: Someone turns up early to a Scottish party.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland, the first visitor to cross the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve (Hogmanay) brings luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish New Year custom of being the year's first visitor to a house.
